Phase 64 plan: docs/phases/version-from-the-source-tree.md @ 61765be. Branch phase/version-from-the-source-tree is STACKED on phase/roadmap-placeholders-are-not-phases (PR #47, approved, unmerged — the arbiter is away); only the last commit is this phase. I will rebase onto main once #47 merges.

Defect: tagteam.__version__ = importlib.metadata.version('tagteam'), which an editable install writes once. Three incidents on 2026-09-20 (issue 2 in docs/tagteam-issues-release-and-venv-upgrade-2026-09-20.md): the arbiter's uv-tool CLI ran 3.14.0 code reporting 3.13.0 — the registry preview printed 'package 3.13.0' and a real sweep would have stamped 41 manifests' provenance field wrongly; this repo's .venv said 3.12.0 for a 3.13.0 tree (two upgrade_smoke failures, environmental, misdiagnosed on two separate days); rankr's link said 0.5.0.

Plan: __version__ prefers the pyproject.toml beside the package when its [project] table declares name = 'tagteam' — true only for a source tree; no such file exists next to a wheel install — else metadata exactly as today, else '0.0.0+unknown'. Regex, not tomllib (requires-python is 3.10). Any read/parse failure falls back; import never raises. Plus 'tagteam --version' / -V / version: 'tagteam X.Y.Z' and the directory it was imported from. framework.package_version(), hook.py, server.py inherit the fix untouched.

Please press on: (1) is 'pyproject.toml one level above the package with name = tagteam' a sound source-tree test — any layout where a wheel install could satisfy it; (2) regex over [project] vs a tomllib-with-fallback; (3) whether stale_egg_info() in upgrade_smoke.py should stay (I keep it: other readers of the metadata are still confused); (4) anything that legitimately wants the *installed metadata* version rather than the tree's — I found none (hook skew warning, cockpit meta tag, manifest stamp all want the running code's version).

Verified: tagteam roadmap check ok (65 phases). No code changed; suite not run (plan cycle).

Approved plan at 61765be. Resolving pyproject.toml relative to the imported package, checking the project name, and preferring its version is appropriate for this repository/source layout; normal installed wheels retain the metadata path. The inspected consumers (framework provenance, hook skew reporting, server version) want the running code version. Keeping stale_egg_info() is reasonable because this change does not update installed distribution metadata.

Implementation guidance:
- cli.main() applies read_only_refusal() before _dispatch(). Add the version aliases to that read-only routing as well as dispatch/help, and test TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1 outside a project. Commands are lowercased there, so account for -V becoming -v internally.
- Treat the regex as a deliberately narrow reader of the release-controlled project table, not a general TOML parser. Anchor name/version assignments to that table; do not pick a tool table version or commented assignment. Missing, ambiguous/duplicate, malformed or unsupported assignments should fall back. Cover invalid UTF-8 too: read_text raises UnicodeError, not OSError. Keep path resolution inside the failure boundary.
- In the wheel test, compare against an independently obtained built version (pyproject or wheel metadata), not another read of tagteam.__version__, so it actually verifies the fallback.
- The name check is a useful layout guard, not proof that no wheel could ever have a same-named pyproject beside it (e.g. unusual --target installs). Ordinary wheel/source layouts are sufficient for this scoped fix; no speculative installation detection is needed.

Reviewed the current initializer, CLI read-only guard/dispatch, release version regex and smoke precondition. No tests run or implementation changes made. The stacked-branch scope is noted.
